Fifth, regarding the classification of the teachings (*panjiao*): one should consider that this sutra’s doctrinal character (*jiaoxiang*) is that of the *Ghee* (*tiedu*), which was revealed through the *Vaipulya* (*fangdeng*) period.
Generally speaking, the Tathāgata’s preaching of the Dharma consists of five periods: first, the *Avataṃsaka*; second, the *Āgama*; third, the *Vaipulya*;

Later, there were those such as the two masters of Gushan and Wuxing; some judged it to belong between the *Prajñāpāramitā* and *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* sūtras, such as Master Huan of Wenling;

"All conditions of form and mind, as well as the mental factors and the objects of those mental factors, are manifested solely by the mind. Your body and your mind are both the wondrous [mind]."

The account of the survival or demise of father and son took a very long time to unfold. Initially, it was said that the woman of the Mātanga clan had led Ānanda into a chamber of lust;

Now, even though the Bhikṣuṇī Śrī actually possessed sharp faculties and swiftly attained the stage of *aśaikṣa*, Yaśodharā’s receipt of the prediction of Buddhahood is in fact recorded in the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*; how could it possibly be otherwise?

It is simply that because the title of this sutra lacks the designation "Prajñā," it cannot be considered identical to the *Prajñāpāramitā*.

[This] is a summary. Question: Although Ānanda is the primary recipient (*pratimukha*) of this present sutra, why is it necessary to explicitly reveal the great purport? Answer:

The second cloud is also called "Protecting the Causes of Kinship.

Third, it is also called "The Definitive Meaning of the Cultivation and Realization of the Tathāgata’s Secret Cause. This refers to the realization of the central doctrine; the "secret cause" is the Perfect [Teaching].

In this sutra, both the opening of understanding and the arousal of practice are accompanied by provisional means (*fangbian*), whereas the clear realization is exclusively perfect (*yuan*).

This is because Ānanda’s initial request contained the phrase "the foremost provisional means"; thus, while his understanding and practice involve expedient means, they are nonetheless distinct from [the provisional].

[This section] selects [the teaching]. However, the primary intent lies solely in the final stage of the Perfect Teaching (yuanjiao), where the stages and positions are clarified as the ultimate destination.

Although both cause and fruit are simultaneously indicated, in reality, the causal mind encompasses the fruit.
The fourth cloud is also titled *Mahāvaipulya-saddharmapuṇḍarīka-rāja-daśadig-buddha-mātṛkā-dhāraṇī-mantra*.
This serves as evidence for its doctrinal character. While "Mahāvaipulya" (Great Vaipulya) appears similar to the *Avataṃsaka*, it is merely identical in meaning;
when considered in terms of chronological sequence, it cannot be classified as belonging to the *Avataṃsaka* proper, but can only be placed above the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*. Wuxing said:

This is the Dharma taught as the Mahāvaipulya. "Mahā" (Great) refers to its essence; "Vaipulya" (Extensive) refers to its function. It is the empty Tathāgatagarbha endowed with the function of non-emptiness.
Furthermore, that which is eternal and pervasive is called "Great"; that which serves as a track and sustains is called "Dharmic" (方); and that which encompasses and enriches is called "Extensive."
These are assigned respectively to the Dharma-body, Prajñā, and Liberation, which are also the three virtues of the Tathāgatagarbha. As stated in the *Zhongjing* (Sutra of the Mean):
"The three characters contain the entirety of essence (*ti*), doctrine (*zong*), and function (*yong*). When these three are unified, one may discuss the characteristics of the teaching.

The name "Wondrous Lotus King" is identical to that of the *Lotus Sūtra*. This present scripture possesses both the provisional and the real; pointing to the provisional as being the real is what is called the "Wondrous Lotus. It unifies...
He is called "King" because he exercises sovereign mastery. Next, the "Dhāraṇī-mantra of the Mother of the Buddhas of the Ten Directions" is the name of the mantra itself.
As stated in the *Vaipulya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*: "This dhāraṇī-mantra can serve as father and can serve as mother.
It further states: "The path of all Buddhas arises from this; it is the father and mother of the Buddhas. The present sutra is precisely the same as that.

Since that sūtra is secretly identical to the Lotus Sūtra, it follows that this present sūtra is likewise secretly identical to the Lotus Sūtra; thus, it is clear that it belongs to the Vaipulya (fangděng) class.

Ānanda has already clarified its revelation and manifestation within the introduction. This means that while the sūtra text itself was secretly identical [to the Lotus], the compilation has now made that identity manifest.

Because there is a hidden identity, one can only realize an explicit identity. It is judged that this sutra is necessarily a Vaipulya (fangděng) text, which, when revealed, constitutes the *amṛta* (tíhú) as its doctrinal characteristic.
The fifth [section] says: "It is also called the 'Mantra of Consecration'; it is the Śūraṅgama of the myriad practices of all Bodhisattvas; you should uphold it."
This is the title of the scripture. Regarding the "Mantras of Empowerment," there are five sections within the Mahāyāna secret canon of Central India.
In the Eastern Vajra Family, Akṣobhya Buddha is the presiding lord;
in the Southern Ratna Family, Ratnasambhava Buddha is the presiding lord; and in the Western Padma Family, Amitāyus Buddha is the presiding lord.

The "Mind-Pinnacle" (*Cittakoṭi*) is also like the investiture of office of a Kṣatriya.

Because the Bodhisattva thereby receives the rank of Buddhahood, the "Śūraṅgama Samādhi" among the myriad practices of all Bodhisattvas should be the name of this sutra. Thus, the former phrase derives its designation from the mantra, yet its meaning extends throughout the sutra;
the latter phrase derives its designation from the sutra, yet its name extends to the mantra. The myriad practices of the Bodhisattva do not go beyond these.
Third, regarding *śamatha-vipaśyanā*: within a single mind that encompasses the three aspects of *śamatha-vipaśyanā*, the myriad practices are fully present.
